summary: Codex is OpenAI's local coding agent, built almost entirely in Rust (688k of 713k main LOC, ~97%) as a 135-crate Cargo workspace (codex-rs) pinned to Rust 1.95.0 / edition 2024, with thin TypeScript and Python SDKs and a Node wrapper package around the released binary. The core stack is Tokio async + Ratatui/crossterm for the TUI, Clap for the CLI, reqwest/rustls(aws-lc) for HTTP, SQLx-managed bundled SQLite for local state, an embedded, sandboxed V8 for 'code mode', tree-sitter for shell parsing, Starlark for exec policies, and OS sandboxing via Landlock/seccomp/bubblewrap. It builds with both Cargo and a heavily customized Bazel (bzlmod) setup, plus pnpm, just, uv/hatchling, and a Nix flake; CI/CD is 27 GitHub Actions workflows with SHA-pinned actions, cargo-deny auditing, and releases published to Cloudflare R2. It talks to the OpenAI API/ChatGPT backend (plus Amazon Bedrock, Ollama and LM Studio as alternative model providers), speaks MCP, gRPC/protobuf, WebSocket and SSE, and reports telemetry via OpenTelemetry/Statsig and crash/feedback data via Sentry. Attention items are all low severity: three crates patched to OpenAI git forks plus two git-rev dependencies, ~20 local patch files applied to third-party Bazel/toolchain modules, and an unpinned openssl-sys = "*" wildcard.

findings.title: Rust 1.95.0 (edition 2024) is the dominant language (~97% of main code)
findings.description: Sokrates counts 687,909 of 712,527 main LOC as Rust (*.rs), making Rust ~97% of the codebase. The toolchain is pinned to stable 1.95.0 via rust-toolchain.toml and all workspace crates use the 2024 edition.

findings.title: Python 3.10+ for the Python SDK, packaging runtime and repo scripts
findings.description: Python (~17.6k LOC per Sokrates) is used for the openai-codex Python SDK (sdk/python), the openai-codex-cli-bin wheel that pins the CLI binary (sdk/python-runtime), and repo maintenance scripts (scripts/). All declare requires-python >= 3.10.

findings.title: TypeScript 5.9 for the @openai/codex-sdk
findings.description: TypeScript is used for the official TypeScript SDK (sdk/typescript), compiled with TypeScript ~5.9 and bundled with tsup into an ESM package. TS/JS is a small share of the repo (~1.5k LOC) since the CLI itself is a Rust binary.

findings.title: Node.js runtime: >=22 for the monorepo, >=16 for the published CLI wrapper
findings.description: Node.js is required for repo tooling and the npm distribution. The monorepo pins Node >= 22 and pnpm >= 10.33, while the published @openai/codex package (a thin bin/codex.js wrapper that launches the native binary) only requires Node >= 16 to maximize installability. The engine skew is intentional but worth knowing.

findings.title: Tokio async runtime
findings.description: Tokio 1.x is the async runtime for effectively the whole Rust workspace (HTTP, WebSocket, gRPC, process management, file watching all run on it), declared once as a workspace dependency.

findings.title: Ratatui + crossterm terminal UI framework
findings.description: The interactive UI (codex-rs/tui, the largest crate) is built on Ratatui 0.30 with a crossterm backend; ansi-to-tui, ratatui-macros and vt100 support it. Crossterm is consumed via an OpenAI fork (see the forked-git-dependencies finding).

findings.title: Clap 4 CLI framework
findings.description: All command-line entry points (codex, codex exec, file-search, etc.) use Clap 4 with derive macros plus clap_complete for shell completions.

findings.title: Axum 0.8 HTTP server framework
findings.description: Axum is used for embedded HTTP servers in several crates (rmcp-client OAuth callback flows, app-server-transport, exec-server, code-mode-host), not for a standalone web application.

findings.title: Embedded V8 JavaScript engine (sandboxed) for code mode
findings.description: The code-mode-runtime crate embeds Google V8 (rusty_v8, pinned =150.4.0, with the v8_enable_sandbox feature) to execute model-generated JavaScript locally. V8 is also built hermetically through Bazel (bazel_dep v8 15.0.245.2) with custom build files under third_party/v8.

findings.title: Test frameworks: cargo test + insta/wiremock (Rust), Jest (TS), pytest (Python)
findings.description: Rust testing uses the built-in harness augmented with insta snapshot testing, wiremock HTTP mocking, assert_cmd, pretty_assertions and divan benchmarks. The TypeScript SDK tests with Jest 29 (ts-jest); the Python SDK uses pytest 8.

findings.title: reqwest HTTP client
findings.description: reqwest 0.12 (with cookie support) is the primary HTTP client for calls to model providers and backend services, wrapped by the codex-http-client crate.

findings.title: rustls TLS stack backed by aws-lc-rs
findings.description: TLS is provided by rustls 0.23 with the aws_lc_rs crypto provider (a dedicated utils/rustls-provider crate configures it), rustls-native-certs for system roots, and tokio-rustls for async streams. Bazel builds link aws-lc as a module. rcgen (also aws_lc_rs-backed) generates certificates.

findings.title: Serde serialization ecosystem
findings.description: serde/serde_json (plus serde_with, serde_yaml, serde_path_to_error, serde_ignored) is the universal serialization layer for protocol messages, config files and persisted state. ts-rs and schemars generate TypeScript types and JSON schemas from the same Rust types.

findings.title: OpenTelemetry + tracing observability stack with OTLP export
findings.description: Structured logging/tracing uses the tracing ecosystem bridged into OpenTelemetry 0.31 (opentelemetry-otlp exporter over tonic/gRPC, tracing-opentelemetry, opentelemetry-appender-tracing). The codex-otel crate centralizes OTLP endpoint and TLS configuration.

evidence.note: workspace declarations for the OTel crates

findings.title: tree-sitter parsers for Bash and PowerShell
findings.description: tree-sitter 0.25 with the bash and powershell grammars is used (e.g. in apply-patch and shell-command) to parse shell commands the agent proposes, which feeds safety analysis and patch application.

findings.title: Starlark interpreter for execution policies
findings.description: The execpolicy crate embeds the starlark-rust interpreter (0.14) so command execution policies can be written in Starlark and evaluated at runtime.

findings.title: gix (gitoxide) for Git operations
findings.description: Git integration (repo state, attribution, history) uses the pure-Rust gitoxide library (gix 0.81) rather than shelling out to git or libgit2, supported by the git-utils crate.

findings.title: OS keyring integration for secret storage
findings.description: The keyring-store crate wraps the keyring crate (3.6) to store credentials in the platform secret service (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, etc.).

findings.title: AWS SDK credential/SigV4 signing crates
findings.description: aws-config, aws-credential-types, aws-sigv4 and aws-types are used by the aws-auth crate to resolve AWS credentials and SigV4-sign requests, enabling the Amazon Bedrock model provider.

findings.title: Cryptography stack: clatter (Noise, post-quantum), ed25519-dalek, crypto_box, age, jsonwebtoken
findings.description: Beyond TLS, the workspace uses clatter 2.2 (Noise protocol with ML-KEM post-quantum options) for secure channels, ed25519-dalek for signing, crypto_box sealed boxes, age for file encryption, jsonwebtoken for JWT handling, and hmac/sha1/sha2/constant_time_eq/zeroize as primitives.

findings.title: OS sandboxing: Landlock, seccomp, bubblewrap, Windows sandbox
findings.description: Command execution is sandboxed per-OS: on Linux via the landlock crate, seccompiler-built seccomp filters and a bwrap (bubblewrap) integration crate; dedicated linux-sandbox, sandboxing, windows-sandbox-rs and process-hardening crates implement the layers. This is a core architectural element of the agent's safety model.

findings.title: Notable smaller Rust libraries (~175 direct workspace dependencies overall)
findings.description: The workspace declares ~175 direct external dependencies. Beyond the majors, notable utilities include anyhow/thiserror (errors), tracing (logging), regex and regex-lite (both present, used for different size/perf tradeoffs), chrono/time, uuid, image, syntect (syntax highlighting), pulldown-cmark (Markdown), symphonia (audio decoding), notify (file watching), portable-pty, sqlx companions, and archive/compression crates (zip, tar, zstd, flate2).

findings.title: TypeScript SDK libraries: zod and the MCP SDK
findings.description: The TypeScript SDK's notable dependencies are zod (schema validation, with zod-to-json-schema) and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk for MCP integration testing/conformance; everything else is dev tooling.

findings.title: Pydantic 2 in the Python SDK
findings.description: The Python SDK's only runtime dependencies are pydantic >= 2.12 for typed models and the pinned openai-codex-cli-bin wheel that ships the native CLI binary.

findings.title: Cargo workspace with ~135 crates and strict clippy policy
findings.description: codex-rs is a single Cargo workspace (resolver 2) of ~135 member crates with centralized workspace dependencies and custom build profiles (dev-small, profiling, ci-test). A large clippy deny-list (including unwrap_used and expect_used) is enforced workspace-wide; cargo-shear is used against unused dependencies.

findings.title: Bazel (bzlmod) hermetic build alongside Cargo
findings.description: The repo has a full Bazel bzlmod setup (MODULE.bazel, rules_rs, hermetic LLVM toolchain, protobuf, aws-lc, v8, openssl and other C deps as modules; custom rules under bazel/ and third_party/; remote-execution config in rbe.bzl). Bazel builds the same Rust code hermetically for CI and cross-platform release, in parallel with plain Cargo for local development.

findings.title: pnpm 10 workspace with supply-chain hardening settings
findings.description: JavaScript packages (codex-cli, responses-api-proxy/npm, sdk/typescript) are managed as a pnpm workspace pinned via packageManager to pnpm 10.33. pnpm-workspace.yaml enables notable supply-chain protections: minimumReleaseAge of 7 days, blockExoticSubdeps, strictDepBuilds and an explicit allowBuilds list.

findings.title: just task runner
findings.description: A root justfile (defaulting to the codex-rs working directory, with a custom Python-based shell shim for cross-platform recipes) is the developer entry point for building, running, formatting and testing.

findings.title: Nix flake dev/build environment
findings.description: A Nix flake (nixpkgs unstable + rust-overlay) provides reproducible dev shells and package builds for Linux and macOS on x86_64 and aarch64.

evidence.snippet: description = "Development Nix flake for OpenAI Codex CLI";

findings.title: Python packaging via uv_build and hatchling
findings.description: The Python SDK builds with the uv_build backend, while the CLI-binary wheel (sdk/python-runtime) uses hatchling with custom build hooks; both configure uv with a 7-day exclude-newer window (supply-chain hardening mirroring the pnpm setting).

findings.title: Linters/formatters: clippy+rustfmt, Prettier, ESLint, ruff, buildifier, codespell
findings.description: Formatting and linting are enforced per ecosystem: clippy and rustfmt (pinned in rust-toolchain.toml) for Rust, Prettier for JSON/MD/YAML/JS repo-wide, ESLint 9 + typescript-eslint for the TS SDK, ruff for Python, buildifier for Starlark/Bazel files (tools/buildifier), and a codespell CI workflow for spelling.

findings.title: GitHub Actions CI: 27 workflows with SHA-pinned actions
findings.description: CI/CD runs entirely on GitHub Actions with 27 workflows covering Rust CI (fast, full, nextest matrix), Bazel builds, SDK/Python builds, issue automation (labeler, deduplicator, translator), CLA, blob-size policy and post-merge checks. Third-party actions are pinned to commit SHAs, a supply-chain best practice.

findings.title: cargo-deny dependency auditing in CI
findings.description: A dedicated cargo-deny workflow audits the Rust dependency tree (advisories/licenses/bans) on every run, complementing the pnpm and uv release-age gates on the JS/Python side.

findings.title: Multi-stage release automation (rust-release, npm, PyPI wheels, R2 publishing)
findings.description: Releases are automated across several workflows: rust-release (+ Windows and zsh variants), python-runtime/python-sdk releases, rusty-v8 prebuilt releases, and publish-r2-release which uploads release assets and metadata to Cloudflare R2 through its S3-compatible API using the AWS CLI.

evidence.snippet: Publish release assets and metadata to R2

findings.title: Docker-based dev containers (Ubuntu 24.04) with DotSlash, including a firewalled secure variant
findings.description: Development environments are containerized: .devcontainer builds an Ubuntu 24.04 image (arm64-targeted), installs Facebook's DotSlash tool distributor as a devcontainer feature, and offers a Dockerfile.secure/devcontainer.secure.json variant with an init-firewall.sh network lockdown. CI also uses a Dockerfile.bazel image.

findings.title: SQLite (bundled) via SQLx for local state
findings.description: Local persistence (state, thread store, message history, audit logs) uses SQLite embedded through SQLx 0.9 with the sqlite-bundled feature and migrations; libsqlite3-sys is deliberately held at a version containing the WAL-reset corruption fix. No external database server is involved.

evidence.snippet: Keep SQLx's bundled SQLite on a version containing the WAL-reset corruption fix

findings.title: Cloudflare R2 blob storage for release distribution
findings.description: Release binaries and metadata are published to Cloudflare R2 object storage (accessed via its S3-compatible API with AWS-named credentials) from a dedicated GitHub environment, making R2 part of the distribution infrastructure.

findings.title: OpenAI API and ChatGPT backend as primary model providers
findings.description: The default model providers call https://api.openai.com/v1 (API-key auth) or the ChatGPT Codex backend at https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex (ChatGPT auth), selected by auth mode in model-provider-info. Numerous auxiliary endpoints under chatgpt.com/openai.com are used for login, connectors and cloud tasks.

findings.title: Amazon Bedrock model provider
findings.description: Amazon Bedrock is supported as an alternative model provider, with requests SigV4-signed via the aws-auth crate and AWS SDK credential resolution.

findings.title: Ollama and LM Studio local model runtimes
findings.description: Dedicated crates integrate local OpenAI-compatible model servers: codex-ollama talks to an Ollama daemon (default http://localhost:11434) including model pulls, and codex-lmstudio manages LM Studio model download and serving.

findings.title: Sentry for feedback/crash envelope upload
findings.description: The feedback crate uses the Sentry Rust SDK (0.46) and a hardcoded DSN pointing at o33249.ingest.us.sentry.io to upload user feedback/diagnostic envelopes.

findings.title: Statsig as a metrics exporter backend
findings.description: The otel crate supports Statsig as an alternative metrics exporter (alongside OTLP), with per-metric disable lists resolved when the Statsig exporter is active; this ties runtime metrics into OpenAI's feature-gating/analytics service.

findings.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP), client and server
findings.description: Codex both consumes and serves MCP: the rmcp-client crate wraps the official Rust SDK (rmcp, pinned =3.1.2) for connecting to MCP servers (stdio and streamable HTTP, with OAuth), the mcp-server/codex-mcp crates expose Codex as an MCP server, and the TS SDK tests against @modelcontextprotocol/sdk with the official conformance suite.

findings.title: gRPC / Protocol Buffers (tonic) for internal service protocols
findings.description: Internal process-to-process protocols are defined in proto3 (code-mode, exec-server relay, thread-config) and served with tonic 0.14 + tonic-prost; protobuf is also wired through Bazel for hermetic codegen.

findings.title: WebSocket transport (tokio-tungstenite)
findings.description: WebSockets (tokio-tungstenite 0.28 with proxy and rustls support, wrapped by the websocket-client crate) carry realtime connections such as the app-server remote-control transport and streaming model sessions. The tungstenite crates are consumed via OpenAI forks (see forked-git-dependencies).

findings.title: Server-Sent Events for model response streaming
findings.description: Streaming responses from model providers are parsed as Server-Sent Events using eventsource-stream in the core client.

findings.title: JSON-RPC-style protocol for the app server
findings.description: The app-server protocol uses a JSON-RPC-like request/response/notification framing over stdio and other transports; the code explicitly notes it is not strict JSON-RPC 2.0 (the jsonrpc field is omitted). Types are shared with TypeScript via ts-rs.

evidence.snippet: We do not do true JSON-RPC 2.0, as we neither send nor expect the

findings.title: OpenAPI-generated backend API models
findings.description: The codex-backend-openapi-models crate holds models generated from an OpenAPI specification of the Codex backend API, indicating OpenAPI as the interface definition format for backend communication.

findings.title: Several dependencies pinned to git forks/revisions instead of crates.io
findings.description: crossterm, tokio-tungstenite and tungstenite are patched to OpenAI-maintained forks (github.com/openai-oss-forks) at fixed revisions, and nucleo (helix-editor git rev) and runfiles (dzbarsky/rules_rust git rev) are pulled directly from git. Pinned revisions keep builds reproducible, but forked/git dependencies do not receive crates.io advisories or normal version bumps and can drift from upstream.
findings.recommendation: Track upstream releases for the forked crates (crossterm, tungstenite family, nucleo) and periodically rebase or retire the forks; ensure cargo-deny advisories still cover the forked code paths.

findings.title: ~20 local patch files applied to third-party Bazel modules and toolchains
findings.description: The patches/ directory carries about 20 .patch files applied via MODULE.bazel to LLVM, rules_rust/rules_rs, rules_cc, v8/rusty_v8, ring, zstd, xz, bzip2 and Windows support modules, plus custom BUILD files under third_party/. This makes hermetic cross-platform builds possible but is a maintenance burden: every module upgrade requires re-validating local patches.
findings.recommendation: Where feasible, upstream the patches to the respective Bazel modules (several look upstreamable, e.g. Windows include-dir fixes) to shrink the local patch set.

findings.title: openssl-sys declared with an unpinned wildcard version
findings.description: openssl-sys is declared as "*" in the workspace dependencies (kept only for platform-specific builds and excluded from cargo-shear). A wildcard range in an application workspace means any future major release would be accepted on a fresh lock, which is unusual next to the otherwise carefully pinned dependency set.
findings.recommendation: Pin openssl-sys to a major version range (e.g. "0.9") to avoid silently adopting a future incompatible release.
